instagram.caption_en:
A tiny brewery in Japan's oldest hot-spring town just walked away from Hong Kong with three medals.

Minakuchi Shuzo, founded in 1895 in Matsuyama on the island of Shikoku, is the only sake brewery still standing in the hot-spring district of Dōgo. At the Oriental Sake Awards 2026 — the first international-standard sake competition held in Asia outside Japan — its Nikitatsu range took silver for NIKITATSU2025, a junmai daiginjo brewed for the brewery's 130th anniversary with Yamada Nishiki rice from young farmers in the Ehime highlands, plus two bronze medals including NIKITATSU2024, made with local Shizuku-hime rice polished to 30% and brewed with Dōgo's own spring water.

The brewery's everyday junmai also made a top-three list of its own: judges paired it with Cantonese stir-fried river shrimp at a tasting held with Hong Kong restaurant Kin's Kitchen. It's the latest medal in a season that already included gold at the Milano Sake Challenge, sixth place at Kura Master in France, and a medal for every label at the International Wine Challenge.
